title: The 1% rule
desc: Risk a small, fixed slice so a losing streak can’t knock you out

cards.title: Ten losses in a row
cards.situation: Your account is $10,000. You risk 10% of whatever is left on every trade. Then you hit 10 losses in a row. Roughly what’s left?

visual.title: 10 losses in a row
visual.label: Ten losses: $10,000 falls to about $9,044 at 1% risk and about $3,487 at 10% risk

options.feedback: Each loss is 10% of a smaller account, so you never quite hit $0. But you’ve lost about two-thirds.
About $3,500 left. You’d need +187% just to get back to even.
That’s what 1% risk would leave. At 10% a trade, each loss is ten times bigger.

cards.work: Each loss takes 10% of what’s left. $10,000 × 0.9¹⁰ ≈ $3,500. At 1% a trade: ≈ $9,040.

cards.title: The 1% rule
cards.text: Many pros risk **1–2% of the account at most** on any one trade. Risk is what you lose if the [[stop-loss|stop]] is hit, not how much stock you buy.

blocks.tip: You can buy $2,500 of stock and still risk only about $100, if your stop is close enough.

cards.title: Survive the losing streak
cards.text: Even good strategies hit losing streaks. Here’s what’s left of $10,000 after a run of losses.

visual.label: What’s left of $10,000 after 5, 10 and 20 losses at 1% and 10% risk

rows.note: Down 10% at 1%. Down 65% at 10%: you’d need +187% to get back.

cards.foot: At 1%, 20 losses in a row leave you down 18%. Bad, but you’re still trading. At 10%, you’re almost wiped out.

cards.title: Bigger bets, faster riches?
cards.myth: Risking more per trade gets you rich faster.
cards.reality: It gets you broke faster too. Losing streaks are normal. Big risk turns a normal streak into a blown account.
cards.rule: pick a risk you could lose 10 times in a row and still keep going.

cards.title: Set your risk
cards.q: Your account is $25,000. Using the [[one-percent-rule|1% rule]], what’s the most you should risk on one trade?

options.feedback: That’s 0.1% of the account. Move the decimal one place: 1% of $25,000 is ten times more.
1% of $25,000. Lose it 10 times in a row and you’re still down only about 10%.
$2,500 is 10% of the account. Ten bad trades like that would cost you most of it.
That’s 4% of the account. A normal losing streak at that size would cut deep.

cards.title: What “risk 1%” means
cards.q: You “risk 1%” on each trade. What does that mean?

options.text: Buy stock worth 1% of the account
options.feedback: The 1% is the loss if the stop is hit, not the size of the position.

options.text: Lose about 1% of the account if the stop is hit
options.feedback: Risk is the loss at your stop. The position itself can be much bigger.

options.text: Aim for a 1% gain on every trade
options.feedback: The rule is about losses, not targets. It caps what one bad trade can take.
It’s not about how often you trade. It caps what you lose if the stop is hit.

cards.headline: You can survive a losing streak.
lines: Risk at most 1–2% of the account per trade.
Risk = what you lose if the stop is hit.
Small risk keeps you in the game through bad runs.
